artifact: R3 Storm match-path increment - acceptance proof
key_discovery: Storm is HALF-BUILT, unlike R1/R2/R4/R5. Storm count (gs.spells_cast_this_turn) + copy-on-resolve already exist at the handler layer (_grapeshot_spell reads spells_cast_this_turn; copies = 1 + storm) and work in GOLDFISH. R3 does NOT add a copy primitive (that would double-count the existing handler). R3 makes the existing storm count REACHABLE + CORRECT + CREDITED on the MATCH path.

narrowing.summary: WANTS_STORM opt-in lives ONLY on the rewritten RubyStormMatchAPL, not the base class.
narrowing.base_class: apl/match_apl.py -> MatchAPL.WANTS_STORM = False. Every other deck inherits False -> the new main-phase-1 damage sync never runs -> bit-identical match path.
narrowing.opt_in_class: apl/ruby_storm_match.py -> RubyStormMatchAPL.WANTS_STORM = True (rewritten from the AUTO_GENERATED stub to cast every spell via gs.cast_spell, payoff last).
narrowing.gate_function: engine/match_runner.py:_storm_match_gate(gs) [either-seat, retained for symmetry]; the ACTUAL main1 damage sync in _simple_play_turn gates on the ACTIVE apl's WANTS_STORM (deliberate active-only, so an opponent's main1 burn is NOT newly propagated inside a storm matchup).

engine_change: ONE new gated surface: a main-phase-1 spell-damage sync in match_runner._simple_play_turn, mirroring _run_post_combat_phase's damage sync. The active view is a fresh GameState (view.damage_dealt starts at 0), so `gs.life_b -= view.damage_dealt` / `gs.damage_to_b += view.damage_dealt` cannot double-count. Gate OFF -> the whole block is a pure no-op. NO new copy primitive, NO change to cast_spell, the goldfish path, _resolve_combat, counter_resolver, or the storm handlers.

wr_anchor.status: NOT separately run at n>=1000 this spike; R3 is fidelity-first (the count/propagation gate is primary, NOT a WR delta). data_quality: medium / APL-tuning-todo.
wr_anchor.note: A LARGE WR jump would be an ABORT signal (likely the free-ritual-mana quirk, see risks), not a win.

risks_and_imperfections_deferred: Ritual net-mana: Desperate/Pyretic Ritual + Manamorphose must produce NET-POSITIVE mana for the chain to reach lethal storm count; if the mana model does not, real-match storm count caps low (tracked, WR under-reads). Do NOT fake it.
Ruby Medallion cost reduction not in _COST_REDUCTIONS (red spells should cost {1} less) -> shorter chain than reality.
Past in Flames recursion (second storm chain) deferred; Pyromancer Ascension spell-doubling deferred.

Generic Storm-keyword coverage: copy is hand-coded per card (Grapeshot/Empty the Warrens/Galvanic Relay); a handler-less storm card copies nothing. A generic primitive is a future gated rung (would double-count the existing handlers if added naively).

General main1-damage-sync gap: 1.2 opens the fix ONLY for storm-opted decks; every other deck's main-phase-1 face burn is still dropped on the match path. The clean ungated fix is a separate broader change needing its own Class-A re-proof.
Optional gated early win-check after the main1 sync (inert for creatureless storm) deferred.
honest_caveats: Storm was already half-built: the storm COUNT + copy-on-resolve were engine-resident for goldfish before R3. R3 does NOT 'add storm to the engine' -- it makes the existing primitive reachable + correct + credited on the MATCH path. The engine change is the gated match-path main1 damage SYNC, not a copy primitive.

The arl_profile change is GATE-VERDICT-identical, NOT literal-JSON-byte-identical: every non-storm deck's confidence + blocking_imperfections are unchanged, but mechanic_counts/evidence gain a new storm:0 key (a value of 0 trips nothing).

Residual detection false-positive surface: a non-storm card whose ORACLE TEXT contains the word 'Storm' could trip the regex fallback (detection uses the keyword list as the primary signal + scans oracle/keywords only, never the card name, so 'Storm Slayer'-type names do not trip). No false positive observed on the tested decks.
Ruby Storm WR under-reads until the ritual net-mana + Ruby Medallion items above are modeled (deferred).
